messages:
Emily Carter: Heads-up — after the kernel swap to `attn_v2` on canary, p99 tail for long sequences jumped ~220ms on pool-east-4. p50/p95 look basically unchanged. KV hit rate unchanged. Suspect interaction between kernel warmup and our queueing (max_wait_ms).

Raj Patel: Can you paste the quick profile and current scheduler config? also which microbatch sizing?

Emily Carter: profile snippet (condensed):
```
reqs: 1200/s
seq_len 8k tail subset (top 1%)
kernel: attn_v2 (rolled 03:12 UTC)
p50: 34ms -> 36ms
p95: 120ms -> 125ms
p99: 380ms -> 600ms
kv_hit: 87% -> 86.8%
queue_delay_p99: 40ms -> 220ms
kernel_switches_per_request: +1.8
```
scheduler config: `max_batch_tokens=2048`, `max_wait_ms=15`, `microbatch_target_tokens=64`.

Mikaela Gomez: interesting — huge jump in queue_delay_p99. attn_v2 probably has slower cold-path for the large attention window. With `max_wait_ms=15` we may be forcing lots of microbatches into separate kernel invocations instead of amortizing.

Raj Patel: tradeoffs: raising `max_wait_ms` reduces #kernel switches and can bring down p99 but increases p50/p90 for latency-sensitive small requests. We should test a sweep: [15, 30, 60, 100]. Also try lowering `max_batch_tokens` to 1536 to avoid very large collect times for huge sequences.

Emily Carter: ran a short canary with `max_wait_ms=60` on pool-east-4 for 10m:
```
p50: 36ms -> 46ms (+10ms)
p95: 125ms -> 130ms (+5ms)
p99: 600ms -> 320ms (-280ms)
queue_delay_p99: 220ms -> 45ms
kernel_switches_per_request: -1.4
```
benefit for p99 is big, p50 regresses but still within our SLO for interactive tier? (we need to check).

Ops Jen: any KV cache regressions or traffic artifacts? KV warmup could explain extra kernel work.

Emily Carter: KV metrics stable; cache TTL and hit ratio unchanged. I sliced traces by KV-hit vs KV-miss and both groups show the same queue_delay jump after the kernel change. So primary axis looks like kernel cold micro-batch warmup and scheduler timing.

Raj Patel: ok. Proposal: implement an adaptive `max_wait_ms` that increases by x2 for requests with seq_len > 2k or when kernel-switch events per window exceed threshold. Also add a short-circuit: if p50 > baseline+Y then revert to lower max_wait for that pool.

Mikaela Gomez: alternative: gate `attn_v2` behind a routing rule for short vs long sequences — route long sequences to attn_v2 only when batch depth >= 2 microbatches. That avoids hurting small requests.

Emily Carter: temp action items I already did on canary:
- sweep `max_wait_ms` = [15,30,60] (done)
- test `max_batch_tokens` 2048 vs 1536 (queued)
- add histogram for kernel_switch_count per request (PR open: #4123)
- flagging runtime to log when kernel fallback occurs to help correlation

perf-bot: Canary results uploaded: https://perf.redwood/dev/reports/1850001234 (summary attached).

Raj Patel: next steps: run 6h sweep on traffic-weighted pools, collect p50/p95/p99 + tail queue_delay + kernel_switch_count. If `max_wait_ms=60` reduces p99 by >150ms while p50 increases <20ms, consider rolling to stable with dynamic knob.

Emily Carter: agreed. also adding a microbench for `attn_v2` cold-path to see if we can optimize kernel warmup (maybe prefetch KV or pre-allocate scratch) — if that helps we can keep `max_wait_ms` low.

Ops Jen: ping security & compliance if we change routing so enterprise tenants don't see regressions.

Mikaela Gomez: noted. I'll add a canary filter to exclude enterprise reserved pools from the initial roll.

Emily Carter: TL;DR: kernel swap exposed scheduler sensitivity. immediate mitigations = sweep higher `max_wait_ms` & lower `max_batch_tokens` for tails, add kernel-switch telemetry, and pursue kernel warmup perf work.

Raj Patel: :eyes: please add the sweep job to the perf dashboard, tag me and ops when you start the 6h run.

Emily Carter: Will do. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
